newsitem.title: UK: Greenalls dips despite 48 pct profit rise.
newsitem.headline: Greenalls dips despite 48 pct profit rise.

text.p: Shares in British pub-to-hotels group Greenalls Plc dipped on Thursday despite a 48 percent jump in the group's full-year profits, towards the top end of analysts' expectations.
By 0852 GMT the stock was down 3p at 599p.
Greenalls posted full year pre-tax profit to end September, excluding exceptionals, of 148.7 million stg.

But the figures exclude the contribution from Boddington, acquired in November 1995, and exceptional items of 31.2 million stg, including 23.9 million of reorganisation costs at Boddington. Underlying profits rose by 10 percent.
Analysts had forecast pre-tax profits between 140 and 150 million stg.
The group said it planned to spend 170 million stg on developing the business in 1996/97, including around 80 million stg on acquisitions and new building.
The group paid a dividend of 15.4 pence, up from 14.2 pence a year ago.
